position: Additional Areas for Reform (The Importance of Space)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the IC and DOD explore better integration of their space assets, examine joint programs and fully use Title 10 and Title 50 authorities jointly for space defense and offense strategies. It also says the IC should support alliances with like-minded partners beyond the Five Eyes, and should refocus space intelligence collection to break down barriers with DOD and embrace commercially derived capabilities, while protecting supply chains and cybersecurity.

status_summary: Executive Order 14369 (signed 2025-12-18, 90 FR 60537) calls for a national security space architecture that integrates commercial space capabilities and for stronger ally and partner contributions to space security, and names the DNI as a consulted party for a missile defense gap report, a space security strategy, an architecture plan and a State-led ally and partner plan due within 90 to 180 days; it does not mention the NRO, the intelligence community as such, joint DOD-IC programs or Title 10 and Title 50 authorities, and the plans' outputs were not found. The Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2026 (Division F of P.L. 119-60, enacted 2025-12-18) has no space, NRO or commercial-imagery provision in its table of contents or the text read. The Space Force and NRO continue joint work on space-based ground moving target indication that began before 2025, with enabling satellites launched and dedicated satellites expected from 2028 (reported 2025-08-05). The FY2026 budget request proposed removing funding for the NRO's commercial radar program and significantly reducing its commercial electro-optical layer, which runs counter to the commercial emphasis; six commercial firms asked Congress in June 2025 to reverse the cuts, the House intelligence committee passed a bill on 2025-09-10 that would restore the commercial imagery funds, and the final FY2026 outcome, which is classified, was not found.

timeline.event: The House intelligence committee passed its FY2026 authorization bill, which would restore the White House cut to NRO commercial imagery funding.

Executive Order 14369, Ensuring American Space Superiority, is signed (published 2025-12-23 at 90 FR 60537), calling for integration of commercial space capabilities and stronger ally and partner contributions, and naming the DNI as a consulted party for a missile defense gap report (90 days), a space security strategy and responsive national security space architecture plan (180 days), and a State-led ally and partner plan (180 days); it does not mention the NRO or the intelligence community as such.

Public Law 119-60 (FY2026 NDAA) is signed; its Division F is the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026. The division's table of contents and the body text read (through Sec. 6703) contain no space, NRO or commercial-imagery provision; Sec. 6621 asks the heads of the NRO, NGA and other elements to develop shared metrics for adopting emerging technology.

title: Integrate IC and DOD space assets, widen allies and embrace commercial space
uncertainties: The final FY2026 appropriation for NRO commercial imagery is a classified line and was not found; the stage may be too low or too high depending on that outcome. The June 2025 Breaking Defense article shows no publication date; its date is the date of the letter it describes. The GMTI program began before 2025, so the 2025 report shows continuation, not a new IC-DOD integration decision. The executive order's 180-day plans were due about mid-June 2026 and their outputs were not found. The August 2025 commercial space executive order (EO 14335) concerns licensing and the Office of Space Commerce and is covered in c21-06. The Space Force offensive and counterspace posture is in c04-20, which also cites EO 14369. Division F of P.L. 119-60 was read on a Senate Intelligence Committee copy of the enrolled text: the table of contents in full and the body through Sec. 6703; the remaining body (Secs. 6704 to 6806) was not seen, but no section title in the table of contents concerns space, the NRO or commercial imagery. The Senate committee bill's plan for a joint NGA-NRO commercial geospatial office (S. 2342, Sec. 325) does not appear in the enacted division's table of contents. The June 2025 firms' letter and the August 2025 general's remarks were removed from the timeline as non-government or descriptive items; their facts remain in the summary with their sources.
